guides.edit:
# Editing Neutre

Neutre is empty on purpose: it is the base that high-fidelity imports write their deck tokens over, so every token it set would show through wherever an imported deck sets nothing.

- Keep its tokens empty. To give decks a look, use deck tokens, or a theme that extends Neutre.
- If it ever sets a token, keep the default pairs readable: ink and ink-muted on bg and surface, on-accent on accent, and component.base.card.highlight-kicker on highlight-bg.
- Keep its namespace `neutre`: imports pin it as the theme of the decks they write.
guides.use:
# Using Neutre

Neutre sets no tokens: a deck on it shows the library defaults, a white bg, near-black ink, a blue accent (#2f5fb3), Libertinus Serif for titles and body, titles 60 and body 32 on a 1920 by 1080 page. High-fidelity PowerPoint imports use it and write the imported deck's own colors, fonts and sizes as deck tokens over it.

- On an imported deck the look lives in the deck tokens, not in Neutre: restyle it there, and keep those tokens.
- Neutre defines only the standard colors (bg, surface, ink, ink-muted, accent, on-accent, rule): a name such as accent-soft or brand-ink does not exist here unless the deck tokens add it.
- Pack components keep their pack defaults: chapter slides on accent with on-accent text, a plain cover with an accent bar, cards on bg with an accent top rule, tables with an accent header.
- As a starting point for a brand, extend Neutre and set only what the brand changes.
